questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature and the cultural experience. Also the country has very interesting ecology, which is why i wanted to do classes within marine ecology. When choosing the destination the courses combined with the nature and culture and ties to Denmark was crucial for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I thought it was a bit difficult to find. The information was spread out a lot on HI website, mobility, KU and mails and it seemed like KU, HI and Erasmus+ wasn't always communicating.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had some intro days where the school, sorroundings and classes were presented, but the way of school was different from KU in terms of changing classes, structuce etc. and this was expected to be understood beforehand. This could be nice to be informed about.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were both student dormetaries, which i stayed at where you had your own room and bathroom but also private housing.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: there were a shared kitchen between 12 people at my dormetary.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I would choose the dormetaries as it's a good way to meet new people while its still affordable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very difficult, as courses were cancelled last minute and i needed to apply for a new pre-approval several times because of this.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: it was a bit difficult to figure out how the credit system worked and which courses were going or not.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I tried to call student service in Iceland but help from Denmark wasn't possible. When i got there student service helped me, but it took some time to find out.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: not very successful. I jumped around a lot of courses to fit my pre-approval, but also because some of the courses were cancelled.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: really look into the courses and be prepared to move around the first few weeks.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: all the courses i did were MA courses. i did 5 different ones. 4 in-class courses and 1 field course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more tied up on being in classs and doing reports, where UCPH is more studying individually and less reports.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- SJAVARVISTFRÆOI, 6 ECTS-point
• CONSERVATION BIOLOGY, 6 ECTS-point
• GLOBAL FISHERIES AND SEAFOOD, 6 ECTS-point
• MARINE PROTECTED AREAS, 4 ECTS-point
• NATURAL HAZARDS AND SOCIETY, 10 ECTS-point.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Conservation Biology. Its super interesting and teaches you a broad range of skills. Also the teacher is great.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: everything is more expensive in iceland. Especially food and accomodation is at least 30% more expensive than Copenhagen.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and housing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were choir, fitness and a lot of events done for the exchange students such as pub crawl and movie nights. especially student cellar is one of the good places where they did a lot of events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go hike, ski and rent/buy a car and do road trips

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend people getting out of Reykjavik and see the nature around. Also do the public pools or explore the cultural possibilites in downtown.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy, as Icelandic culture is a lot like danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: yes, go to town and local music bars such as Röntgen, 12 Tonar etc. also talking to other students at campus and be open-minded.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the language was different and they are a bit more reserved until you get to know them.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the local pools which is a big part of the culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the great nature, use the public pools and try to get Icelandic friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's more expensive than you would think and i would get a car to get the most out of your exchange.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: doing a surf/splitboard trip around the northern part of Iceland.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: going through a personal rough time back home while being away.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
